reason: README/get_started.md gives an evaluation command for pretrained Swin-T that can run on CPU with a small ImageFolder dataset, no credentials needed.
demo: get_started.md Evaluation: python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node 1 main.py --eval --cfg configs/swin/swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224.yaml --resume swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224.pth --data-path <imagenet>
goal: Get the Swin-T ImageNet-1K evaluation from get_started.md working on CPU only (the code assumes CUDA/NCCL so it needs CPU adaptation). Download the pretrained swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224.pth from the README Model Zoo link and run main.py --eval with configs/swin/swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224.yaml on a small ImageFolder-style dataset (data-path/train and data-path/val with class subfolders, e.g. a few generated images). It must finish and print the 'Accuracy of the network on the N test images' line.
check: A hidden test generates a tiny ImageFolder dataset, downloads the Swin-T checkpoint, runs the eval command via torch.distributed.run on one process, and checks the log reports accuracy over all 16 test images.
